items.title: USCIS resets EB-5 fees and codifies the program’s 2022 statutory changes
items.summary: USCIS finalized new fees for requests under the EB-5 immigrant-investor program, codified provisions of the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022, and implemented related statutory requirements. The agency says it revised both its fee study and the technology fee after comments on the 2025 proposal. The rule takes effect November 30; applications, petitions, and requests postmarked on or after that date must include the new fees.

items.title: NHTSA rewrites fuel-economy standards for model years 2022 through 2031
items.summary: NHTSA’s final SAFE Vehicles III rule amends Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards for passenger cars and light trucks covering model years 2022–2026 and 2027–2031. It also changes vehicle classification and other compliance pathways. The agency characterizes the revisions as a statutory recalibration responsive to market demand; that is its policy judgment, not an empirical finding established by the notice itself. The rule becomes effective November 30.

items.title: Most metropolitan unemployment rates fell, while payroll growth remained narrowly distributed
items.summary: BLS reports that August unemployment rates were lower than a year earlier in 234 of 387 metropolitan areas, higher in 126, and unchanged in 27. Yet nonfarm payroll employment rose significantly in only nine areas, fell in five, and was statistically unchanged in 373. Washington–Arlington–Alexandria recorded the largest absolute payroll decline, down 66,000. These metro figures are not seasonally adjusted and combine household- and establishment-survey measures.

items.title: Second-quarter GDP is revised sharply upward, while purchase prices still rise rapidly
items.summary: BEA’s third estimate puts second-quarter real GDP growth at a 2.2% annual rate, 0.7 percentage point above the second estimate, principally because investment, consumption, and government spending were revised upward. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers grew 4.6%, while the gross-domestic-purchases price index rose 5.6%. State GDP increased in 44 states and the District of Columbia, ranging from 4.0% in New York to –2.3% in West Virginia.

items.title: August spending outpaced income as the personal saving rate fell to 4.1%
items.summary: BEA estimates that August personal income rose 0.2% and disposable income 0.3%, while personal consumption expenditures increased 0.9%; inflation-adjusted consumption rose 0.6%. The personal saving rate was 4.1%. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased 0.3% during the month and 3.4% from a year earlier; the corresponding core rates were 0.2% and 3.0%. This release incorporates annual revisions extending back to January 2021.

items.title: Electric-vehicle electricity use kept growing in 2026, but at a markedly slower rate
items.summary: EIA estimates that light-duty electric vehicles used nearly 14 billion kilowatthours in the first half of 2026, 8% more than in the second half of 2025 but below the 13–24% half-year growth recorded recently. New electric-vehicle sales fell 19% over the same comparison. The agency links the slowdown to expiring federal tax credits, while noting that its electricity-use series is modeled from external data rather than collected through its conventional surveys.

items.title: Treasury issues temporary rules for creating and funding Trump Accounts
items.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury and Internal Revenue Service
items.summary: Treasury and the IRS issued temporary regulations for Trump Accounts, the new individual retirement accounts for eligible minors created by the 2025 tax law. The rules cover Treasury’s automatic establishment of an initial account, elections by other responsible parties, rollovers, reporting, and qualified general contributions from governments or tax-exempt organizations to defined classes of beneficiaries. The regulations took effect September 30; materially identical proposed regulations were published concurrently for comment.

items.title: GAO finds unsupported and misattributed savings on DOGE’s Wall of Receipts
items.summary: In a recently identified August audit, GAO examined DOGE’s claimed $110 billion in contract, grant, and lease savings as of July 7. It found undisclosed methods, insufficient information to verify 96% of reported grant savings, 108 leases already being phased out before DOGE existed, and a claimed $1.7 billion contract saving where no termination or reduction occurred. DOGE did not respond; GAO recommended prominent disclosure of the data’s limitations.

items.title: CBO prices the Senate version of the snow-water forecasting program at $15 million
items.summary: CBO estimates that the Senate committee version of H.R. 3857 would cost $15 million over 2026–2031, assuming appropriation of the authorized amounts. The bill would reauthorize and modify the Bureau of Reclamation’s interagency snow-monitoring and water-supply forecasting program, authorizing $3 million annually for 2027–2031. CBO estimates no direct-spending or revenue effect and no public- or private-sector mandates; a House version previously authorized substantially more per year.

items.title: Linked records show suicides comprised nearly two-thirds of violent deaths captured in 2023
items.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
items.summary: CDC’s linked 2023 surveillance data cover 72,093 violent deaths in the 50 states and District of Columbia: 62.4% suicides, 28.5% homicides, and the remainder chiefly deaths of undetermined intent. Firearms were involved in 58.6%. The system represented 91.6% of nationally counted violent deaths in its covered categories, but California, Florida, and Texas supplied detailed records only for selected counties; Puerto Rico’s 730 deaths were analyzed separately.

items.title: Biphoton correlations produce confocal optical sectioning without scanning or pinholes
items.publisher: Euan Millar, Emma Pearce, Daniele Faccio, and Miles J. Padgett
items.summary: This optics preprint reports a wide-field imaging system in which spatial coincidence measurements of entangled photon pairs suppress out-of-focus light, creating confocal sectioning across the field without a physical pinhole or point-by-point mechanical scan. The authors report an axial response √2 narrower than classical confocal imaging, attributed to position–momentum entanglement. The result is an author-reported experimental demonstration in a preprint, not yet evidence of routine biological or clinical performance.

items.title: A new public reforecast dataset concentrates high-resolution weather cases on consequential events
items.summary: The reGRAF preprint documents 1,836 GPU-generated weather reforecasts selected mostly around high-impact events from 2004–2024. Its global mesh refines to roughly four kilometers over the United States, Caribbean, and Europe and fifteen kilometers elsewhere; most fields appear every fifteen minutes through a 27-hour forecast. The nonrandom event-heavy sampling broadens difficult cases but is not a representative continuous climatology. The authors have released the Zarr-format data through the AWS Open Data Initiative.
